You are playing the part of the person described below, on foot. Decide as this person would.

Below you are told what you can see and hear around you right now. Say what you do from now on: how you move.
Left and right always mean your own left and right.
Other people see how you move, if you are in their view. Nobody else knows your intent or your reason.

HOW TO REPLY
Reply with a single JSON object and nothing else, with these keys in this order:
"intent": what you are trying to do, in your own words.
"steps": what you do from now on, as a list of steps (see STEPS). Write [] if you carry on as you are.
"reason": why, in your own words. Nobody else sees it.
The format, with placeholders: {"intent": "<what you are trying to do>", "steps": [<step>, ...], "reason": "<why>"}

STEPS
The steps are carried out in order, each beginning when the one before it ends, unless it has a start that has not come yet: then it begins when its start comes, and until then you walk on towards where you are going. After the last step ends, you walk on towards where you are going. Each step is a JSON object with these keys; leave out the ones you do not need:
"start": in any step, when it begins: "now", {"at_distance_m": <metres>} to begin when the person you would meet is that close to you, or {"after_seconds": <seconds>}, counted from now. Without it, the opening step begins now and a later step begins when the one before it ends.
"speed_mps": the speed you walk at during the step, in m/s, from 0 (standing still) up to the fastest you can walk.
"turn": {"to": "left" or "right", "degrees": <from 0 to 90>}: during the step, walk at this angle to your left or right of the direction you are going.
"back_up_m": walk backwards this many metres. The step ends when you have.
"until": when the step ends: {"seconds": <seconds>}, {"at_distance_m": <metres>} to end it when the person you would meet is that close to you, or one of these events, written as its name in quotes: "other_passes" (until the other person has passed you), "other_stops" (until the other person stops) or "i_am_out_of_the_stretch" (until you are out of the narrow stretch). Every step needs it, except a step that walks backwards.
The format of a step, with placeholders: {"start": "now", "speed_mps": <number>, "turn": {"to": "<left or right>", "degrees": <number>}, "until": {"seconds": <number>}}

ABOUT YOU
- You are 25 years old.
- You are a man.
- You are on your way to the supermarket.
- You are walking at 1.30 m/s. Your usual walking speed is 1.30 m/s.
- The fastest you can walk is 2.00 m/s.
- Your body is 0.50 m wide.
- You are walking with a cane.
- You are easy-going and tend to give way.

WHERE YOU ARE
- You are in a passage 1.75 m wide. The wall on your left is 0.77 m from you, the wall on your right 0.98 m.

WHO YOU CAN SEE
- Person 1, 9.8 m away, straight ahead of you: walking in the opposite direction to you.
  They look about 25 years old.
  They look like a woman.
- Person 2, 9.8 m away, straight ahead of you: walking in the opposite direction to you.
  They look about 25 years old.
  They look like a woman.

At your current speeds you would meet Person 1 in about 3.8 s.

What do you do now? Reply with the JSON object only.

{"intent": "Keep to the right side of the passage so the women coming toward me can pass, giving them room.", "steps": [{"start": "now", "speed_mps": 1.30, "turn": {"to": "right", "degrees": 10}, "until": {"at_distance_m": 3.0}}, {"speed_mps": 1.20, "until": {"seconds": 4.0}}], "reason": "I'm easy-going and give way; stepping slightly to my right keeps the left side open for the two people walking toward me, and I can slow a little while using my cane."}

Stepping out of the role now. Earlier, as this person, you:
- decided: "Keep to the right side of the passage so the women coming toward me can pass, giving them room."
  Your steps were: [{"start": "now", "speed_mps": 1.3, "turn": {"to": "right", "degrees": 10.0}, "until": {"at_distance_m": 3.0}}, {"speed_mps": 1.2, "until": {"seconds": 4.0}}].
Was what you did based on anything: a law or official guidance, a published study, a local custom, a habit, or nothing in particular? If you know a specific source, name it. If there is none, say so. That is a perfectly good answer.

HOW TO REPLY
Reply with a single JSON object and nothing else, with these keys:
"basis": in your own words, what you did was based on.
"kind": one of "law_or_guidance", "published_study", "local_custom", "habit", "common_sense" or "none".
"source": a specific source you know of, as a citation, or "none".
"applies_to": which of your decisions this is about.
The format, with placeholders: {"basis": "<what it was based on>", "kind": "<one of the kinds>", "source": "<a citation, or none>", "applies_to": "<which decision>"}
